stories.title: 📜 Gospel of Nicodemus (Acts of Pilate)
summaryBullets: The Jewish leaders bring Jesus before Pilate, accusing him of sorcery and claiming to be the Son of God and king of Israel.
Pilate questions Jesus, who gives measured answers while remaining silent at times.
Witnesses speak of Jesus’ miracles — healing the sick, raising the dead, and feeding the multitudes.
Pilate is struck by the accusations and asks if these things are true, finding no fault in him.
Pilate sends Jesus to Herod, fulfilling jurisdictional protocol; Herod questions him but Jesus does not answer.
Witnesses testify that Jesus healed the lame, gave sight to the blind, cleansed lepers, and cast out demons.
Others recount how he raised Lazarus and Jairus’ daughter, confirming his power over death.
Herod and Pilate acknowledge his extraordinary works, but the leaders continue pressing for his execution.
Pilate resists condemning Jesus, declaring he finds no guilt, but the Jewish leaders pressure him with threats of reporting to Caesar.
The crowd shouts for Jesus’ crucifixion; Pilate symbolically washes his hands to show he is innocent of the decision.
Jesus is sentenced, mocked, beaten, and led away to be crucified.
While on the cross, supernatural signs occur — darkness falls and the earth trembles.
After the crucifixion, Joseph buries Jesus in a tomb and a stone is rolled across the entrance.
Soldiers are stationed at the tomb by order of the leaders to prevent the body being stolen.
At dawn, a great earthquake occurs; an angel descends in dazzling light and rolls back the stone.
The guards witness the event and report what they saw, but are bribed with money to say the disciples stole the body.
In Hades, the patriarchs, prophets, and righteous souls wait for deliverance.
Adam and his descendants lament their captivity, longing for the promised Redeemer.
Satan and Hades argue about Jesus, with Satan boasting of causing his death and Hades fearing the power of the coming one.
Prophets like Isaiah and John the Baptist testify that the Christ is near and will soon descend to rescue them.
A great voice is heard, and the gates of Hades tremble at the approach of Christ.
The bronze gates and iron bars are shattered as the King of Glory enters.
Christ binds Satan and strips him of authority, casting him into chains.
The angels proclaim, 'Lift up your gates, O rulers, and be lifted up, you everlasting doors.'
Christ takes Adam by the hand and raises him up, declaring victory over death.
The patriarchs, prophets, and righteous follow: David, Isaiah, John the Baptist, and others are freed.
They rejoice as Christ leads them out of Hades and into paradise.
The gates of paradise open, and the redeemed enter in triumph.
The rulers and elders hear the guards’ account of the angel and resurrection, but suppress it with bribes.
Testimonies circulate among the disciples and witnesses that Christ descended to Hades and rose victorious.
The narrative closes with exhortation to proclaim the victory of Christ’s resurrection and liberation of the righteous.
crossRefs: Luke 23:1–2 — Leaders accuse Jesus before Pilate.
John 18:33–38 — Pilate questions Jesus, finds no fault.
Matthew 27:12–14 — Jesus remains silent before accusations.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כָּשַׁף (kāšap̱) — Greek: φαρμακεία (pharmakeía) — Aramaic: כשפים (kešāfîn)
translationNotes.note: Term often used by opponents to describe miracles negatively, framing divine works as magical deception.

stories.keyTakeaway: Jewish leaders accuse Jesus before Pilate, but testimony about his miracles complicates their charges.
